p0.original: 关键问题：我们如何形成记忆
p0.en: Question: How do we make memories?

p2.original: 记忆有三个阶段。尽管每个阶段的编码和存储记忆的方式各不相同，但它们共同合作将感觉经验转化为具有某种模式或意义的持久性记录。
p2.en: There are three stages to memory. While the way each phase is coded and stored is different, they work together to translate perceived experience into a persistent record of some type or significance.

p3.original: 如果你想让一次讲座中的信息成为你永久性记忆的一部分，那么它就必须经过三个连续阶段的加工：首先是感觉记忆阶段，然后是工作记忆阶段，最后是长时记忆阶段。这三个阶段的工作就像一条流水线，将接连不断输入的刺激转换成人们可以存储和随后可以重构的有意义的模式（Atkinson & Schiffrin，1968）。这个三阶段模型最初由理查德·阿特金森（Richard Atkinson）和理查德·谢夫林（Richard Schiffrin）提出，在经过一些细化和修改后，现在已被广泛接受。图5-4展示了信息如何在这三个阶段流动（请注意：不要把这三个阶段与我们前面提到的记忆的三项基本任务混淆。）
p3.en: If you want the information in a lecture to be part of your permanent memory, it has to go through three successive stages: first, the sensory memory phase, then the working memory phase, and finally, the long memory phase. These three phases of work are like a streaming line, which converts successive input of stimulus into meaningful models that can be stored and subsequently re-engineered (Atkinson & Schiffrin, 1968). The three-stage model, originally proposed by Richard Atkinson and Richard Schiffrin, has now been widely accepted, with some refinements and modifications. Figure 5-4 shows how information flows through these three stages (please note that these three stages are not confused with the three basic tasks of memory that we mentioned earlier). I don't think so.

p5.original: 注：记忆通常被分为三个加工阶段。所有最终进入长时记忆的信息都必须先经过感觉记忆和工作记忆的加工。
p5.en: Note: Memory is usually divided into three processing stages. All information that eventually enters a long memory must be processed first through both the sensory memory and the work memory.

p6.original: 感觉记忆（sensory memory）是这三个加工阶段中最短暂的，它通常只能将视像、声音、气味、质地和其他感官印象保存几秒的时间。虽然感觉记忆一般只在无意识层面上运作，但你可以在移动的手电筒或7月4日[1]旋转的烟火所留下逐渐消退的光痕中看到它的效果。当听一段旋律时，你也可以在一个音符融入另一个音符的过程中听到感觉记忆消退的效果。总体来说，这些短暂的图像所维持的时长仅够我们的工作记忆从接收到的感觉信息中筛选出重要的信息。
p6.en: Sensory memory is the shortest of these three processing phases, and it usually saves only a few seconds of visual, sound, smell, texture and other sensory impressions. Although the sensory memory usually works only at the unconscious level, you can see its effects in the motion flashlight or in the faded light left by the spinning fireworks on 4 July. And when you listen to a melody, you can also hear the effect of feeling memory fades while one note is integrated into another. In general, these short images are only sufficient to keep our work memory alive to filter important information out of the sensory information that we receive.

p7.original: 工作记忆（working memory）是信息加工的第二阶段，它能选择性地从感觉登记中获取信息，并将之与已经存储在长时记忆中的信息建立起联系。（当我们说“这听起来很耳熟”时所表达的就是这种联系。）工作记忆保存信息的时间一般为20～30秒（Nairne，2003），这使得它可以作为一个有效的缓冲器，暂时保存你刚刚听到的名字或者遵循别人刚刚给你的指示。最开始的时候，心理学家将这个阶段称为短时记忆（short-term memory，STM），这个命名反映了当时的心理学家认为这一阶段仅仅是一个短期的、被动的存储箱的观念。然而，许多研究发现，在这个阶段有多个主动的心理过程飞速地加工着信息，因此就产生了形容该阶段的新术语——工作记忆。
p7.en: Working memory is the second stage of information processing, which selectively captures information from the perception register and links it to information already stored in long-term memory. This is the kind of connection that we express when we say, “This sounds familiar”. The working memory is usually kept for 20-30 seconds (Nairne, 2003), which allows it to serve as an effective buffer, temporarily preserve the name you have just heard or follow the instructions you have just been given. At the beginning, the psychologist referred to this phase as short-term memory (short-term memory, STM), a name that reflected the perception of the then psychologist that this phase was only a short-term, passive storage box. However, many studies have found that there are several active psychological processes processing information at this stage, thus creating a new term for describing the phase — working memory.

p8.original: 长时记忆（long-term memory，LTM）是信息加工的最后一个阶段，它从工作记忆中接收信息，并能长时间地存储信息——有时能存储一生的时间。长时记忆中存储的信息包括我们有关这个世界的所有知识，从母亲的面孔到你最喜欢的歌曲的歌词，再到心理学家和精神病医生之间的区别都囊括其中。这一学习阶段的核心概念简要概括了这三个阶段：
p8.en: Long-term memory (long-term memory, LTM) is the final stage of information processing, receiving information from working memory and storing it for long periods of time — sometimes for life. The information stored in the long memory includes all our knowledge of the world, from the face of the mother to the lyrics of your favorite song, to the distinction between psychologists and psychiatrists. The core concept of this learning phase provides a brief overview of these three phases:

p9.en: There are three stages to memory. While the way each stage is coded and memory stored varies, they work together to translate perceived experience into a persistent record of some kind of pattern or significance.

p10.original: 这一学习阶段将重点阐述每个阶段对最终记忆产物的独特贡献（见表5-1）。更具体地说，我们在之后的内容中将从存储容量、持续时间（保持信息的时长）、结构和功能以及生物基础等方面来介绍每个阶段。

More specifically, each phase will be described in our subsequent content in terms of storage capacity, duration (the duration of maintaining information), structure and functionality, and biological base.

p18.original: 解释感觉记忆的作用和局限性。
p18.en: Explaining the role and limitations of sensory memory.

p19.original: 你的感觉器官收集的信息远比你所能用到的要多。当你在读这本书的时候，你其实在接收许多信息，包括纸张上的所有文字、房间里的声音、皮肤上衣物的触感、空气的温度、胃里有点饥饿的感觉等。大脑如何处理如此众多的感觉输入呢？
p19.en: Your sensory organs collect much more information than you can use. When you read this book, you're actually receiving a lot of information, including all the text on the paper, the sound in the room, the touch of the skin, the temperature of the air, the feeling of hunger in the stomach, etc. How does the brain handle so many sensory inputs?

p20.original: 感觉记忆的作用就是将传入的感觉信息保持一定的时间，仅仅够你的大脑快速扫描并决定需要注意哪些信息流。但是感觉记忆到底能存储多少信息呢？认知心理学家乔治·斯珀林（George Sperling）设计了一个非常简单却十分巧妙的心理学实验来回答这个问题。
p20.en: The function of a sense memory is to keep the information that is being sent in for a certain period of time, just enough for your brain to scan fast and decide what information flow needs attention. But how much information can you store in your senses? A cognitive psychologist, George Sperling, designed a very simple, yet very clever psychological experiment to answer this question.

p21.original: 就像这些烟花留下的轨迹一样，感觉记忆只能将传入的感觉信息保持一小会儿。
p21.en: Just like the trails left by these fireworks, the memory can only keep the information that's going on.

p22.original: 5.2.1 感觉记忆的容量和持续时间
p22.en: 5.2.1 Capacity and duration of sensory memory

p23.original: 斯珀林证明了感觉记忆可以容纳比意识所能觉察到的多得多的刺激信息。他首先要求人们尽可能地记住在屏幕上闪现不到1秒的一组字母。
p23.en: Sperin has demonstrated that a sense of memory can accommodate much more stimulating information than consciousness can perceive. He first asked people to remember, as far as possible, a set of letters that appeared on the screen for less than one second.

p27.original: 不出所料，呈现不到1秒的话，大多数人只能记住3或4个字母。
p27.en: As expected, if less than one second is present, most people can only remember three or four letters.

p28.original: 但是，斯珀林想知道，有没有可能有远比这3个或4个字母更多的信息进入临时记忆缓冲器，却在能够被报告之前就消退了？为了检验这个猜想，他修改了实验任务，流程如下。字母阵列在屏幕上闪现后，一个声音会马上出现以提示被试要报告哪一行字母：高音表示报告最上面一行，中音表示报告中间一行，低音则表示报告最下面一行。因此，在看到短暂呈现的字母序列并听到哔声后，被试无须再报告所有字母，而是只需立即报告其中一行字母即可。
p28.en: However, Splin wondered whether there was a possibility that much more information than these three or four letters could enter the temporary memory buffer, but it had faded before they could be reported. In order to test this assumption, he modified the experimental mission, which follows. When the letter array appears on the screen, a sound emerges immediately to indicate which line letter is tried to report: the high is the top line of the report, the middle is the middle line of the report and the low is the bottom line of the report. Therefore, when a short series of letters is seen and beeps are heard, it is not necessary to report all the letters, but only one line of them immediately.

p29.original: 在这种部分报告的条件下，无论提示报告哪一行，大多数人都能达到近乎完美的准确率。也就是说，斯珀林实验中的被试可以准确地报告，但不能报告出全部的三行字母。这一结果表明，感觉记忆的实际存储容量可以达到12个或以上，即使现实中被试表现为除了3～4个字母外，其他字母通常都在进入意识之前就从感觉记忆中消失了（Sperling，1960，1963）。
p29.en: Under such partial reporting conditions, the majority of the population is able to reach near-perfect accuracy rates, regardless of the line in which the report is directed. That is, the tests in the Splin experiment were able to report accurately, but not all three lines of letters. This finding shows that the actual storage capacity of the sensory memory can reach 12 or more, and even if the reality is to be tested as having disappeared from the sensory memory before it entered consciousness, with the exception of three to four letters (Sperling, 1960, 1963).

p30.original: 如果我们的感觉记忆持续的时间能更长，从而让我们有更多时间来扫描感觉信息，这样会不会更好呢？答案可能是不会。随着新信息不断进入，旧信息需要迅速消失，以免记忆系统过载。我们的记忆系统生来就保证感觉记忆能持续足够长的时间，可以让不同的信息相互融合，使我们体验到流畅感和连续性。幸运的是，感觉记忆通常又不会持续过久，不至于干扰新的感觉印象。
p30.en: Would it be better if we had more time for our feelings and memories, so that we could have more time to scan the information? The answer may not be. As new information continues to enter, old information needs to disappear quickly to avoid overloading memory systems. Our memory systems are born to ensure that the memory of the feeling lasts long enough to allow for the convergence of different information and allow us to experience fluidity and continuity. Fortunately, the sense of memory usually does not last long enough to interfere with the new impression.

p31.original: 5.2.2 感觉记忆的结构和功能
p31.en: 5.2.2 Structure and function of sensory memory

p32.original: 你可能觉得感觉记忆就像大脑中的电影屏幕，图像被快速地投射到上面，然后消失。事实上，正是感觉记忆中图像的融合给了我们“电影”（motion picture）中人物与画面在运动的感觉，但电影实际上只是一系列快速呈现的静止图像。
p32.en: You may feel like a movie screen in your brain, and the images are projected quickly up there and disappear. In fact, it's the combination of images in the sense that gives us a sense of people and images in the motion picture, but movies are actually just a series of fast-moving static images.

p33.original: 但并非所有的感觉记忆都由视觉图像组成。我们对每种感觉都有一种独特的感觉登记（sensory register），每种感觉登记都如图5-5所示的那样记录着不同种类的感觉信息。
p33.en: But not all of the sensory memories are made up of visual images. We have a unique sense of being registered for each feeling, each recording different kinds of feeling information, as shown in figures 5-5.

p34.original: 图5-5 感觉记忆转化为工作记忆的过程
p34.en: Figure 5-5: The process of translating sensory memory into working memory

p35.original: 注：只有一小部分被感觉记忆捕获的信息转移到了工作记忆中，并在工作记忆阶段被赋予意义。
p35.en: Note: Only a fraction of the information captured by the sensory memory is transferred to the work memory and given meaning at the work memory stage.

p36.original: 值得注意的是，就像数字图像对相机来说没有意义一样，感觉记忆中的图像并没有被赋予任何意义。感觉记忆的工作就是简单地存储图像。将感觉赋予意义是下个阶段工作记忆的任务。
p36.en: It is worth noting that just as digital images are meaningless to the camera, images in the sense of memory are not given any meaning. The job of feeling memories is simply to store images. The task of giving meaning to the feeling is to remember the work at the next stage.

p38.original: 感觉记忆的生物基础似乎很简单。在这一记忆加工的开始阶段中，记忆图像的表现形式是感觉器官和它们通往大脑的神经通路中的神经活动。因此，感觉记忆是由我们感觉系统中那些快速消退的刺激痕迹组成的（Bower，2000b；Glanz，1998）。然后，工作记忆会“读取”这些逐渐消失的感觉痕迹，并决定哪些会被注意，哪些会被忽略和消失。
p38.en: The biological basis for feeling memory seems to be simple. At the beginning of this memory processing, memory images are expressed in the form of neuroactivity in the sensory organs and their neuropaths to the brain. So, the sense memory is made up of the rapid retreating irritation in our system (Bower, 2000b); Glanz, 1998. The work memory then “reads” these disappearing impressions and determines which will be noticed, which will be ignored and which will disappear.

p41.original: 评述工作记忆的加工过程、功能和局限性。
p41.en: Processes, functions and limitations of reviewing work memory.

p42.original: 在记忆加工的第二阶段，工作记忆充当一个临时的存储场所，存储你刚听到的一个新名字，或者当你在阅读一句话的后半部分时，临时存储这句话的前半部分。更广泛地说，工作记忆是意识经验的处理器，加工来自感觉记忆的信息，以及从长时记忆中提取的信息（Jonides et al.，2005）。所有事物都通过工作记忆进入意识。
p42.en: In the second phase of the memory processing, working memory serves as a temporary storage site for a new name you just heard, or for the first half of a sentence when you read it. More broadly, work memory is a processor of conscious experience, processing information from sensory memory and extracting information from long-term memory (Jonides et al., 2005). Everything goes to consciousness through work memory.

p43.original: 此外，工作记忆提供了一个存在于脑海中的“工作空间”，在将信息进行更持久的存储之前，我们在这里对它们进行分类和编码（Shiffrin，1993）。在此过程中，我们将长时记忆中的信息与感知经验相结合，从而赋予其意义。例如，工作记忆是一个存在于头脑中的文件夹，当你为明天的考试复习时可以从中提取昨天课堂上所学的内容。
p43.en: In addition, working memory provides a “workspace” in mind, where we classify and code information before it is stored more permanently (Shiffrin, 1993). In doing so, we combine the information in our memory with the sensory experience, thus giving it meaning. For example, work memory is a folder in your mind from which you can extract what you learned yesterday in class when you are studying for tomorrow's exams.

p44.original: 你可以把工作记忆看作整个记忆系统中的“中央处理芯片”。在这一角色中，工作记忆通常会将信息保存20～30秒，这远比感觉记忆持续的时间要长。如果你格外努力地复述信息，那么它保持的时间会更久。例如，在你将一个新电话号码存入你的通讯录之前，不断地重复这个号码。工作记忆也是头脑中的工作空间，我们会在其中有意识地琢磨从长时记忆中提取的想法和图像，这一过程被称为思维。因此，在所有这些角色中，工作记忆不仅是心理活动的中心，还起着保持其他记忆成分之间联系的作用。
p44.en: You can see the work memory as a "central processing chip" in the entire memory system. In this role, working memory usually keeps information for 20 to 30 seconds, which is much longer than feeling memory. If you try harder to repeat the information, it will last longer. For example, you keep repeating a new phone number before you deposit it in your address book. Work memory is also a workspace in the mind, where we consciously reflect on ideas and images drawn from long-term memory, a process known as thinking. Thus, in all these roles, working memory is not only central to psychological activity, but also serves to maintain links between other memory components.

p45.original: 5.3.1 工作记忆的容量和持续时间
p45.en: 5.3.1 Capacity and duration of work memory

p46.original: 心理学家乔治·米勒（Miller，1956）曾提出一个著名的观点，记忆第二阶段的容量是“神奇数字”7±2个。他想表达的意思是，工作记忆大约能存储7个项目。最新的研究表明，我们的工作记忆容量甚至更低，仅能存储3到5个项目（Cowan，2010）。不管具体的数字是多少，工作记忆的存储容量的确因人而异，所以如果你想知道自己的记忆容量，那么你可以做一下“试一试”版块中的测试。
p46.en: The psychologist, George Miller, 1956, had made a famous point that the second phase of memory had a capacity of 7 ±2 “magic numbers”. What he wanted to say was that the work memory could store about seven projects. Recent studies have shown that our work memory capacity is even lower and that we can store only three to five projects (Cowan, 2010). Whatever the number, the storage capacity of the work memory does vary from person to person, so if you want to know your memory capacity, you can do a test in the "tried" section.

p47.original: 试一试 测量你的工作记忆容量
p47.en: Try and measure your working memory.

p48.original: 请看下面的数字列表，首先浏览第一行的四个数字。不要尝试去记住它。只是快速阅读；然后把视线从书上移开，并试着回忆刚才阅读的数字。如果你记对了，就继续看下一行更长的数字，直到你开始出错为止。你的工作记忆能记住的最长数字串是哪个？其中包含几个数字？
p48.en: Look at the list of numbers below, and first look at the four numbers in the first row. Don't try to remember it. Just read quickly; Then you move your eyes off the books and try to remember the numbers that you just read. If you remember correctly, keep looking at the next line longer until you start making mistakes. Which is the longest number you can remember from your work? How many numbers are there?

p57.original: 测试的结果就是你的数字记忆广度，或者你对数字信息的工作（短时）记忆容量。研究表明，在理想的测试条件下，大多数人都可以记住5到9个数字。如果你能记得更多，那么你可能使用了“组块”这一特殊技巧。
p57.en: The result of the test is the breadth of your digital memory, or the capacity of your work on digital information. Research shows that under ideal test conditions, most people can remember 5 to 9 figures. If you remember more, you might use the special technique of "groups."

p58.original: 当我们的工作记忆过载时，原先存储的旧项目通常会不断地减少以容纳新项目进入。然而，当工作记忆中都是需要关注的信息时，我们就无法注意到进入感觉的新信息。许多专家认为，这就是为什么有限的工作记忆容量会导致我们在开车时使用手机很危险（Wickelgren，2001）。事实上，研究发现，当我们驾驶汽车并在此期间用手机通话时——即使在免提模式下——我们也只能加工大约50%的感觉输入的信息。超过四分之一的（累计超过130多万起）交通事故是由司机边开车边使用手机造成的，并且开车时发信息会使你撞车的概率增大约26倍（National Safety Council，2013）。
p58.en: When our work memory is overstretched, old items previously stored are usually constantly reduced to accommodate new projects. However, when the work memory is filled with information that requires attention, we cannot notice new information that enters the feeling. Many experts believe that this is why the limited work memory capacity makes the use of mobile phones dangerous when driving (Wickelgren, 2001). In fact, the study found that when we drive a car and talk on a mobile phone during that time — even in a no-motion mode — we can only process about 50 per cent of the information that is imported. More than one quarter (over 1.3 million in cumulative numbers) of traffic accidents are caused by the use of mobile phones by drivers, and the transmission of information while driving increases the probability of crashes by about 26 times (National Safe Council, 2013).

p59.original: 需要注意的是，就存储容量来看，工作记忆明显小于感觉记忆。事实上，工作记忆的容量在这三个记忆阶段中是最小的。这种容量的限制，再加上有限的保存信息的时间，使工作记忆成为记忆系统的信息“瓶颈”（见图5-6）。工作记忆所存储的容量有限和持续时间短的双重问题使得学生加工和记忆讲座或教科书中的大量信息变得尤为困难。幸运的是，我们在接下来的内容中将会看到解决这些困难的办法。
p59.en: It is important to note that, in terms of storage capacity, the work memory is significantly smaller than the sensory memory. In fact, the work memory is the smallest of these three memory stages. This capacity limitation, combined with a limited amount of time to preserve information, makes working memory an information “bottleneck” for memory systems (see figure 5-6). The dual problem of limited capacity and short duration of work memory makes it particularly difficult for students to process and remember a large amount of information in lectures or textbooks. Fortunately, we will see solutions to these difficulties in the next section.

p61.original: 注：工作记忆位于感觉记忆与长时记忆这两个阶段之间，其容量比感觉记忆和长时记忆要小得多，这使得工作记忆成为记忆系统中的信息瓶颈。最终，很多来自感觉记忆的信息输入都在工作记忆阶段消失了。
p61.en: Note: Work memory lies between the two stages of sensory memory and long-term memory, with a much smaller capacity than sensory memory and long-term memory, making it an information bottleneck in memory systems. Ultimately, many of the messages from the sensory memory have disappeared during the working memory phase.

p62.original: 组块和组块法 在记忆中，组块指的是任何信息模式或有意义的信息单元。它可以是一个字母或数字，一个名字，甚至是一个概念。例如，字母P-H-I-L本可以构成四个组块，但是你可能会将其识别为一个名字，所以你可以将这4个字母组合成一个组块。因此，组块法（chunking）可以帮助你将更多信息放入工作记忆的7个槽道。
p62.en: Group and block method In memory, block refers to any information mode or meaningful information unit. It can be a letter or a number, a name, even a concept. For example, the letters P-H-I-L could have constituted four blocks, but you might have identified them as a name, so you could have combined them into one block. So, the blocking method helps you put more information into the seven channels of your work memory.

p63.original: 电话公司多年前就开始利用组块法。当它们最初将一个电话号码的7个数字（例如，8675309）组合成两个较短的数字串（867-5309）时，它们就是在帮助我们将7个单独的项目存储为2个组块——现在，我们只需要多记一个组块就能记住电话号码中新加入的区号。美国政府使用同样的组块原理来帮助人们记住9位数的社会保险号码。同样地，如果你去超市时没有列清单，你可以将你需要购买的物品进行分类，如蔬菜类、奶制品类和罐头食品类。
p63.en: The telephone company used the block method many years ago. When they initially combined seven numbers of a telephone number (e.g., 8675309), into two shorter series (867-5309), they were helping us store seven separate items into two blocks — now we need only one extra block to remember the new number added to the telephone number. The United States Government uses the same block principle to help people remember the nine-digit social security number. Similarly, if you go to the supermarket without a list, you can classify the items you need to buy, such as vegetables, dairy products and canned foods.

p64.original: 复述的作用 想象你在点比萨时，询问你的室友们想要什么样的配料。当你给比萨店打电话时，为了让室友选择的配料留在你的工作记忆中，你可能会一遍又一遍地重复这个清单。这种方法被称为保持性复述（maintenance rehearsal），它通过防止其他竞争信息的输入帮助我们暂时将信息保持在意识中。尽管人们经常会尝试这样做，但是重复并不是将信息转化为长时记忆的有效方法。因此，使用这种策略来为考试做准备是行不通的。
p64.en: Recapitulating the role of imagine you asking your roommates what kind of ingredients they want when you have a bit of pizza. When you call the pizza store, you may repeat the list over and over again to keep the ingredients selected by the roommate in your work memory. This method, known as maintenance rehearsal, helps us keep information in consciousness for the time being by preventing other competitive information from being entered. Although this is often attempted, duplication is not an effective way of translating information into long-term memory. It is therefore not feasible to use such a strategy to prepare for the examination.

p65.original: 更好的策略是使用精细复述（elaborative rehearsal）。通过这种方法，信息不仅被重复，而且能主动地与已经存储的知识联系起来。其中一种方法是把一个新想法与一些你在逻辑性基础上能想到的东西相联系。当你读到回声记忆是听觉感觉记忆的一个术语时，你是否认为“这很有道理，因为回声就是与声音有关”？另一种方法是思考与概念有关的个人化的例子。例如，当你在上一部分学习“组块”这一概念时，试着回想一下你使用该策略帮助自己记住一长串项目的经历，这种精细复述在提高记忆力方面非常有效。这里有一个关于精细复述的警告：在你为一些事实建立关系网之前，请先确保你已经清楚地了解了这些事实！举例来说，如果你错误地认为记忆就像一台摄像机，并思考如何让它合理，那么你就是在强化错误的记忆。同样，如果（在本章开头提到的案例中）唐娜的治疗师让她想象她的父亲可能有机会猥亵她的情景，那么仅仅想象那些事情就可能会让唐娜创造出错误的记忆（Loftus，1997；Zaragoza et al.，2011）。
p65.en: A better strategy is to use fine rehearsals. In this way, information is not only duplicated but also proactively linked to stored knowledge. One way is to link a new idea to something that you can think of on a logical basis. When you read echo memory as a term for hearing and feeling memory, do you think that “it makes sense, because echoes are about sound”? Another approach is to reflect on individualized examples of concepts. For example, when you learn about the concept of “clusters” in the last part, try to recall your experience of using that strategy to help you remember a long list of projects, a fine recapitulation that is very effective in enhancing memory. Here is a warning about the fine recapitulation: before you build a network of facts, make sure you have a clear understanding of them! For example, if you wrongly think that memory is like a camera and think about how it makes sense, you're reinforcing the wrong memory. Similarly, if Donna's therapist (in the case mentioned at the beginning of this chapter) had allowed her to imagine that her father might have had the opportunity to molest her, then simply imagine that something might have allowed Donna to create the wrong memories (Loftus 1997); Zaragoza et al., 2011).

p66.original: 5.3.2 工作记忆的结构和功能
p66.en: 5.3.2 Structure and function of working memory

p67.original: 我们在这一学习阶段的开始向你介绍工作记忆的概念时就已经提及，它的名字反映了这一阶段记忆加工的主动性。那么工作记忆参与了哪些活动呢？目前，研究人员艾伦·巴德利（Allen Baddeley）及其同事（Baddeley，2007；Baddeley & Hitch，1974）认为，工作记忆主要参与四种活动：中央执行器、语音环路、视空间模板和情景缓冲器。接下来，我们将仔细探讨每一种活动（见图5-7）。
p67.en: As we mentioned at the beginning of this learning phase, we introduced to you the concept of working memory, whose name reflects the initiative of the processing of memory at this stage. So what kind of activities does the work memory involve? Currently, the researcher Allen Baddeley and his colleague (Baddeley, 2007); Baddeley & Hitch, 1974) considers that working memory is mainly involved in four activities: central implementer, voice loop, visual space templates and scenario buffers. Next, we will look closely at each activity (see figure 5-7).

p69.original: 注：巴德利（2003）的工作记忆模型更新版，包括分配注意的中央执行器，加工视觉和空间信息的视空间模板，加工声音的语音环路，以及可以将多种信息组合成记忆事件的情景缓冲器。
p69.en: Note: Update of the working memory model in Badli (2003), including a central implementer assigned attention, visual space templates for processing visual and spatial information, voice loops for processing sound, and scenario buffers that can combine multiple types of information into memory events.

p70.original: 中央执行器 中央执行器是工作记忆的信息交换中心，将你的注意导向到从感觉记忆和长时记忆输入的重要信息上，并与大脑的自主（有意识）反应系统相连接。即使是现在，当你坐着阅读这一学习阶段的内容时，工作记忆中的中央执行器也在帮助你决定是注意书中的词汇，还是注意从其他感觉传入的其他刺激，抑或是注意从长时记忆中提取的想法。
p70.en: The central implementer, the clearing house for working memory, directs your attention to vital information from sensory memory and long-term memory input, and connects it to an autonomous (conscious) response system of the brain. Even now, when you sit and read the content of this learning phase, the central implementer in your work memory helps you decide whether to take note of the words in the book, or of the other incentives that come from other feelings, or of the ideas taken from the long-term memory.

p71.original: 听觉编码：语音环路 当你读到像“呼呼”“砰砰”“布谷”和“哗哗”这样的词时，你能在脑海中听到它们所描述的声音。这种听觉编码（acoustic encoding）也会出现在那些非拟声词上。也就是说，不管是我们是在阅读时看到这些词汇，还是在听演讲时通过耳朵听到这些词汇，工作记忆会将我们接触到的所有词汇都转换成口语的发音，并将它们纳入语音环路（Baddeley，2001）。在语音环路中，工作记忆在加工这些词汇时会保持这些言语模式的听觉（声音）形式。
p71.en: Hearing code: Voice loops, when you read words like "hoo-hoo-hoo-hoo-hoo-hoo-hoo-hoo-hoo-hoo-hoo-hoo-hoo-hoo-hoo-hoo, you can hear the voices they describe in your head. This hearing code (acoustic encoding) will also appear on those unwritten statements. In other words, whether we read these words or hear them through our ears when we listen to them, the work memory translates all the words we encounter into spoken pronunciations and includes them in the voice loop (Baddeley, 2001). In the speech loop, working memory maintains the audio (sound) form of these speech patterns when processing these words.

p72.original: 听觉编码会产生独特的记忆错误。当人们回忆他们刚刚看到的字母表时，他们往往会将发音相似（如D和T）而不是外观相似（如E和F）的字母相互混淆（Conrad，1964）。然而，撇开可能产生的记忆错误不谈，听觉编码具有独特的优势，特别是在学习和使用语言方面（Baddeley et al.，1998；Schacter，1999）。
p72.en: Hearing coding can create unique memory errors. When people recall the alphabet that they have just seen, they often confuse the letters that sound similar (e.g. D and T) rather than look similar (e.g. E and F) (Conrad, 1964). However, aside from possible memory errors, hearing codes have unique advantages, particularly in terms of learning and using languages (Baddeley et al., 1998); Schacter, 1999.

p73.original: 视觉和空间编码：视空间模板 工作记忆的视空间模板在加工视觉和空间信息中发挥着基本相同的功能，它对空间中物体的视觉图像和心理表征进行编码。当你试图回忆自己把车钥匙放在哪里时，它保持着你在脑海中到处翻找的视觉图像；它还保持着你从家到学校所用的心理地图。神经科学的相关证据表明，视空间模板的运行需要包括额叶和枕叶在内的多个大脑系统之间的协作。
p73.en: Visual and spatial coding: The visual space template for working memory functions essentially the same way in processing visual and spatial information, which encodes visual images and psychological manifestations of objects in space. When you try to remember where you put the car keys, it keeps the visual images that you look around in your head; It also maintains the psychological map you use from home to school. Relevant evidence from neuroscience suggests that the operation of space templates requires collaboration between multiple brain systems, including foreheads and pillows.

p74.original: 信息捆绑：情景缓冲器 巴德利工作记忆模型中新增了情景缓冲器，它的作用是将工作记忆中的单个信息碎片（如声音、视觉信息和其他感觉输入信息）捆绑成一个连贯自洽的情景。通过这一过程，情景缓冲器充当一个当前信息的临时存储设施，与此同时我们将其与长时记忆中的信息进行比较，这有助于加深我们对当前信息的理解。情景记忆使我们能够记住电影和其他事件的故事情节，因为它提供了一个将视觉、空间、语音和时间顺序等方面的信息组织成一个可记忆情景的场所（Baddeley，2003）。
p74.en: Information bundling: A scenario buffer was added to the Bardley working memory model to bind individual pieces of information in the working memory (e.g. sound, visual and other sensory input) into a coherent and self-conforming scenario. Through this process, the scenario buffer serves as a temporary storage facility for current information, while we compare it with information in long-term memory, which helps to deepen our understanding of current information. Scenario memory allows us to remember the storylines of films and other events, as it provides a venue where information about visual, spatial, voice and time sequences can be organized into a memoryable scenario (Baddeley, 2003).

p75.en: 5.3.3 Level of processing of work memory

p76.original: 有一个重要的技巧：在工作记忆阶段，你在新信息和已有知识之间建立的联系越多，你就越有可能在以后回忆起这个信息。很明显，这需要工作记忆与长时记忆之间的相互作用。根据弗格斯·克雷克（Fergus Craik）和罗伯特·洛克哈特（Robert Lockhart）提出的加工水平理论（levels-of-processing theory），“深度”加工使新信息与长时记忆建立起更多的联系，使新信息变得更富有意义且更容易记忆（Craik & Lockhart，1972）。下面用一个著名的实验（见图5-8）来说明这一点。
p76.en: There is an important skill: at the work memory stage, the more you connect new information and existing knowledge, the more likely you will be to remember that message later. Clearly, this requires interaction between working memory and long-term memory. According to Fergus Kraik and Robert Lockhart's theory of processing levels, the “deep” processing has made new information more relevant and easier to remember (Craik & Lockhart, 1972). This is illustrated by a well-known experiment (see figures 5-8).

p77.original: 图5-8 加工水平影响记忆效果
p77.en: Figure 5-8 Process levels affect memory effects

p78.original: 深度加工是最好的记忆技巧，你可以将其应用到自己的学习中！你可以将概念用自己的语言表达出来，就像你要把这个概念教给那些不了解它的人一样，从而实现对你想要学习的信息进行深度加工的目的。从你自己的生活中寻找例子来解释这个概念，这种精细复述的方式，也可以帮助你对概念进行更深度的加工。
p78.en: Deep processing is the best memory technique you can apply to your own learning! You can express the concept in your own language, just as you want to teach it to those who don't know it, so that you can do the in-depth processing of the information you want to learn. Looking for examples from your own life to explain the concept, this finely recapitulated approach can also help you to process it more deeply.

p80.original: 将加工水平理论应用到你的学习过程中
p80.en: Applying the process level theory to your learning process.

p81.original: 根据你在克雷克和塔尔文（Tulving）的实验中所学到的，考虑一下对你自己学习实践的启示。比较学生常用的在材料上标记重点与在材料上做笔记这两种策略。从加工水平的角度来看，你预测哪种策略能更好地记忆材料的内容？为什么？如果你在做笔记，你应该照抄教材中的要点，还是把它们翻译成你自己的话？请解释你的选择。
p81.en: Based on what you learned in your experiments in Crack and Tulving, consider the inspiration for your own learning and practice. Compare the strategies commonly used by students to mark priorities on materials and to take notes on materials. From a processing level point of view, what strategy do you predict to better remember the content of the material? Why? If you're taking notes, should you copy the main points of the course or translate them into your own words? Please explain your choice.

p83.original: 尽管有些细节尚不清楚，但工作记忆可能是在神经回路中以反复闪现信息的形式来存储信息。脑成像结果显示，额叶皮层的脑区参与工作记忆的加工过程（Beardsley，1997；Smith，2000），进而将工作记忆中的信息投射到大脑的所有感觉区域，以及那些参与长期存储的脑区。脑成像结果还表明，额叶有一些解剖学上独特的“执行加工”，这些执行加工将注意集中在短期存储的信息上（Smith & Jonides，1999）。这些脑区共同分配注意，设定信息加工的优先级，制订计划，更新工作记忆中的内容，并且监控事件发生的顺序。
p83.en: Although some details are not yet clear, the working memory may be stored in the form of repeated flashes of information in a nervous loop. The results of the brain imaging show that the cortex's brain is involved in the processing of the work memory (Beardsley, 1997); Smith, 2000), which projectes the information in the work memory into all the sensory areas of the brain, as well as those that are involved in long-term storage. The results of brain imaging also show that there are a number of anatomically unique “executive processes” of the lobe, which will focus on information stored in short-term storage (Smith & Jonides, 1999). These brain regions share attention, set priorities for information processing, develop plans, update the work memory and monitor the sequence of events.

p86.original: 描述长时记忆的结构、功能和生物基础。
p86.en: Describe the structure, function and biological basis of long-term memory.

p87.original: 你还记得是谁发现了经典条件反射吗？你会骑自行车吗？你过了多少次生日？这些信息和你所知道的其他知识，都存储在你的长时记忆中，长时记忆是记忆三阶段模型中的最后一个阶段。
p87.en: Do you remember who found the classic reflex? Do you know how to ride a bike? How many birthdays have you had? All this information and all the other knowledge you know is stored in your long memory, which is the last of the three-stage model.

p88.original: 考虑到存储在长时记忆中的海量数据，我们能够如此轻松地提取其中的大部分数据简直就是奇迹。很明显，如果有人问你的名字，你不必仔细检索整个人生的记忆信息就能找到答案。这种神奇现象的产生得益于长时记忆所具有的一个独特特征：长时记忆中的词汇和概念是基于它们的意义来编码的。反过来，这又能它们与其他具有类似意义的项目联系起来。相应地，你可以将长时记忆想象为一个相互关联的巨大网络。因此，良好的提取线索（促进长时记忆激活的刺激）可以在记忆网络中进行导航，帮助你在所有的存储数据中快速地找到所需的项目。
p88.en: Given the amount of data stored in memory over time, it is a miracle that we can extract most of them so easily. Obviously, if someone asks you your name, you don't have to search carefully for the memory of life to find the answer. The creation of this magical phenomenon has benefited from a unique feature of long-term memory: the words and concepts of long-term memory are coded on the basis of their meaning. This, in turn, links them to other projects of similar significance. In turn, you can imagine long-term memory as a huge interconnected network. Therefore, good extraction leads (irritation for long-term memory activation) can navigate in memory networks and help you quickly find the required items in all stored data.

p89.original: 5.4.1 长时记忆的容量和持续时间
p89.en: 5.4.1 Capacity and duration of long-term memory

p90.original: 有多少信息可以被存储在长时记忆中？目前来看，长时记忆拥有无限的存储容量。（还没有人达到存储极限，所以你不必通过减少学习内容来节约长时记忆的容量。）长时记忆可以存储毕生的信息：从工作记忆中输入的所有经验、事件、信息、情绪、技能、词汇、类别、规则和判断。因此，长时记忆中包括了你对世界和自我的全部知识。这使长时记忆在持续时间和存储容量上成为记忆的三个阶段中理所当然的冠军。但是长时记忆是如何拥有无限容量的呢？这是记忆研究领域的另一个未解之谜。也许我们可以把长时记忆看作一种心理“脚手架”，所以当你建立的联系越多时，它能容纳的信息也就越多。
p90.en: How much information can be stored in long-term memory? At present, memory has unlimited storage capacity. (No one has reached the storage limit, so you don't have to save long memory by reducing the amount of learning. Long-term memory can store life-long information: all experiences, events, information, emotions, skills, vocabulary, categories, rules and judgements entered from work memory. Thus, your entire knowledge of the world and of yourself is included in the long memory. This makes memory the rightful champion of the three stages of memory in terms of duration and storage capacity. But how can long memory have unlimited capacity? This is another puzzle in the field of memory research. Maybe we can look at long-term memory as a psychological scaffold, so the more you connect, the more information it can hold.

p91.original: 5.4.2 长时记忆的结构和功能
p91.en: 5.4.2 Structure and function of long-term memory

p92.original: 在全面地了解了长时记忆后，我们来看看长时记忆的两个主要组成部分。
p92.en: After a comprehensive understanding of the long memory, we look at two main components of the long memory.

p93.original: 1. 其中一个组成部分是程序性记忆（procedural memory），它存储着我们知道事情应该如何做的信息。
p93.en: 1. One of the components is procedural memory, which stores information that we know what to do.

p94.original: 2. 另一个组成部分是陈述性记忆（declarative memory），它存储着我们能够进行描述的信息，即我们知道的事实或记得的经历。
p94.en: 2. Another component is the representational memory, which contains information that we can describe, that is, the facts we know or the experiences we remember.

p95.original: 因为一些脑损伤患者可能只会失去长时记忆中的一种记忆而保留另一种记忆（正如我们之后将提到的），所以我们知道程序性记忆和陈述性记忆是两种不同的记忆。
p95.en: Because some people with brain damage may simply lose one memory in a long memory and preserve another (as we will mention later), we know that procedural and narrative memory are two different memories.

p96.original: 程序性记忆 当我们骑自行车、系鞋带或演奏乐器时都会调用程序性记忆。事实上，我们一直在使用程序性记忆存储我们所有的熟练技能的心理指南或者“程序”（Schacter，1996）。
p96.en: Procedural memory, when we ride a bicycle, tie a shoelace, or play an instrument, calls procedural memory. In fact, we have been using procedural memory to store psychological guides or “procedures” of all our skills (Schacter, 1996).

p97.original: 很多程序性记忆的运转在意识之外进行：只有在训练的早期阶段，当我们必须专注于我们所做的每一步时，才会有意识地思考自己行为表现的细节。随后，在我们彻底习得这项技能后，它的运转基本上是在意识之外，就像音乐会上的钢琴家在演奏乐曲时，并不需要有意识地回忆每个音符（图5-9应该能帮助你厘清长时记忆的两个主要组成部分之间的关系）。
p97.en: Many of the procedural memories work out of consciousness: only at an early stage of training, when we have to focus on every step we make, will we consciously think about the details of our behaviour. Then, after we have thoroughly learned this skill, it operates largely out of consciousness, as the piano at the concert plays the music without having to remember each note in a conscious manner (figures 5-9 should help you to clarify the relationship between the two main components of your long memory).

p98.original: 程序性记忆，类似于一些人所说的“肌肉记忆”，它是根深蒂固、不易遗忘的。即使你已经很多年没骑自行车了，如果你过去知道怎么骑车，大概率你现在仍然会骑。
p98.en: Procedural memory, similar to what some refer to as “muscle memory”, is deep-rooted and unforgettable. Even if you haven't been riding a bike for years, if you used to know how to ride a bike, probably you still can.

p99.original: 陈述性记忆 我们用陈述性记忆来存储事实、对事物的印象和经历过的事件。当你回忆心理学中的主要观点或你最难忘的假期时，就需要依赖陈述性记忆。与程序性记忆相比，使用陈述性记忆通常需要付出有意识的心理努力，正如你所看到的那样，人们在试图回忆事实或自己的经历时会转动眼球或做出某种面部表情。
p99.en: We use narrative memories to store facts, impressions of things and events that we've experienced. When you recall the main points of psychology or your most memorable vacation, you need to rely on narrative memory. The use of narrative memory, as compared to procedural memory, usually requires conscious psychological effort, as you can see, when trying to remember facts or experiences, people turn their eyes or make some kind of facial expression.

p100.original: 更复杂的是，陈述性记忆本身有两个主要的组成部分，即情景记忆（episodic memory）和语义记忆（semantic memory）。情景记忆负责处理个人经历中那些丰富的细节（如初吻），而语义记忆只存储不包含“我还记得那时……”这种上下文的信息，如乘法口诀表或国家首都的名称等。
p100.en: More complex is the fact that narrative memory itself has two main components, namely, scenario memory and semantic memory. Scenario memory handles the rich details of personal experience (e.g. first kiss), while semantic memories store only information that does not contain “I remember that time...” such context, such as a multiplication list or the name of the national capital.

p101.original: 1. 情景记忆存储你对自己生活中的事件或“情景”的记忆。它还存储对事件的时间编码（或时间标记）和环境编码，以确定事件发生的时间和地点。例如，当你把最近度假的经历或者一段不愉快的恋情存入情景记忆时，你也会将这些事件发生的时间和地点的编码一并存储到记忆中。就这样，情景记忆充当了你内心的日记或自传体记忆。当有人问你“元旦前夕你在哪里”或者“上周二你上课时做了什么”时，你可以查阅情景记忆来回答这些问题。
p101.en: The scenario memory memory stores your memory of events or “situations” in your life. It also stores the time (or time mark) and environment codes for events to determine the time and place of events. For example, when you put the recent experience of vacation or an unpleasant relationship into the memory of the scenario, you also store the coding of the time and place of these events. So, the scenario memory serves as a diary or autobiography of your heart. When someone asks you, "Where were you on New Year's Eve" or "What did you do in your class last Tuesday," you can look at the situational memory to answer these questions.

p102.original: 2. 语义记忆是陈述性记忆的另一个组成部分（如果你对此感到困惑，请参见图5-9），它存储着词汇和概念的基本含义。通常，语义记忆不会保留获取相应记忆内容时的时间和地点信息。因此，你会将“猫”的概念保存在语义记忆中，但你可能记不起你第一次学会“猫”这一词义时的情景。在这方面，语义记忆更像一部百科全书或一个数据库，而非一部自传。它存储了大量关于姓名、面孔、语法、历史、音乐、礼仪、科学原理和宗教信仰的事实信息。你知道的所有事实和概念都存储在语义记忆中，当有人问你“美国第三任总统是谁”或“陈述性记忆的两个主要部分是什么”的时候，你可以通过查阅语义记忆获得答案。
p102.en: 2. Semantic memory is another component of narrative memory (see figure 5-9 for your confusion), which contains the basic meanings of terminology and concepts. Semantic memory usually does not retain information about the time and place of acquisition of the corresponding memory content. So you'll keep the concept of the cat in semantic memory, but you probably don't remember the first time you learned the term "cat." In this regard, semantic memory is more like an encyclopedia or a database than an autobiography. It stores a great deal of factual information about names, faces, grammar, history, music, protocol, scientific principles and religious beliefs. All the facts and concepts you know are stored in semantic memories, and when someone asks you, “Who is the third president of the United States” or “What are the two main parts of the narrative memory”, you can get answers by looking at semantic memories.

p103.original: 图5-9 长时记忆的组成部分

p104.original: 注：陈述性记忆包含你知道的特定信息，即知道“是什么”。它存储事实、个人经历、语言、概念等一切我们可能会说“我记得”的信息。程序性记忆包含你知道“如何做”的记忆，尤其是运动技能和行为学习的记忆。
p104.en: Note: The narrative memory contains specific information that you know, namely, what is known. It stores all the information that we might say “I remember”. The procedural memory contains the memory of how you know how to do it, especially in terms of motor skills and behavioural learning.

p105.original: 图式 当你去上课、在餐厅吃饭、打电话或参加生日聚会时，你知道接下来可能会发生什么，因为所有这些事件都发生在你熟悉的场景。认知心理学家将其称为图式（schema）：一种存储于语义记忆中的知识集，它为我们提供理解事件的背景信息（Squire，2007）。当然，虽然图式包含的确切内容与文化背景和个人经历有关，但这里强调的是我们可以通过调用图式来让新的经历变得有意义。
p105.en: When you go to class, eat at the restaurant, make phone calls or party birthdays, you know what's going to happen next, because all these events happen in the scene you know. Cognitive psychologists refer to it as a map (schema): a collection of knowledge stored in semantic memory, which provides us with background information on understanding events (Squire, 2007). Of course, while the exact content of the diagram is related to cultural background and personal experience, it is emphasized here that we can make new experiences meaningful by using the diagram.

p106.original: 图式能帮助我们快速获取信息。因此，当有人说起“生日聚会”时，你可以立即利用图式中的信息告诉自己，你所期望的生日聚会与吃蛋糕和冰淇淋、唱《生日快乐》歌、拆礼物等内容有关。同样重要的是，当你调用自己的“生日聚会”图式时，你并不需要对记忆中与之不相关的知识进行筛选。例如，在“上课”图式或“在餐馆吃饭”图式中所包含的信息。你可以通过完成“试一试”版块中的内容，感受图式是多么有用。
p106.en: The diagrams help us get information quickly. So when someone talks about a birthday party, you can immediately use the information in the graphic to tell yourself that the birthday party you want is about cake and ice cream, singing Happy Birthday songs, breaking presents, etc. Equally important, when you call your own birthday party, you don't have to filter the unconnected knowledge in your memory. For example, information contained in “class” or “dinners in restaurants”. You can feel how useful the pattern is by completing what's in the "test" section.

p107.original: 试一试 图式如何影响记忆
p107.en: How does the pattern affect memory?

p108.en: . The pattern in the act example.

p109.original: 请仔细阅读下面这个段落：

p110.original: 住院部主任琼斯一边调整他的面罩，一边焦急地查看着被固定在他面前的那张长桌上的苍白身躯。他用那又小又尖的器械迅速地划了一下，一道细细的红线就出现了。接着，那个急切的年轻助手小心地将开口扩大，另一个助手推开表面泛着白光的脂肪，使重要的部位能够显露出来。每个人都惊恐地盯着这个因长得太大而无法切除的丑陋的东西。琼斯现在知道继续下去是没有意义的。
p110.en: The head of the hospital department, Jones, adjusted his mask while anxiously looking at the pale body of the long table that was fixed in front of him. He drew with that tiny, sharp device quickly, and a fine red line appeared. Then the eager young assistant carefully expanded the opening, and the other assistant pushed the fat out of the surface with white light, so that important areas could be revealed. Everyone is scared to stare at this ugly thing that can't be removed because it's too big. Jones now knows there's no point in continuing.

p111.original: 现在，请在保证不看旁边段落的前提下完成下面的练习。
p111.en: Now, please complete the following exercise without looking at the next paragraph.

p112.original: 请回忆段落中是否出现过下列词汇：
p112.en: Please recall whether the following terms have appeared in the paragraphs:

p113.original: 病人 手术刀 血液 肿瘤

p114.original: 癌症 护士 疾病 手术

p115.original: 在最初的研究中，大多数阅读了这个段落的被试都标记了“病人”“手术刀”和“肿瘤”这几个词汇。你是否也标记了这些词汇？然而，这些词汇都没有在段落中出现过！
p115.en: In the initial study, most of the tests that read the paragraph marked the terms “patient” “scalter” and “tumour”. Did you mark those words? However, none of these terms have appeared in the paragraphs!

p116.original: 虽然将上述故事解读为一个医学故事会使它更容易被理解，但这也会导致被试对内容不准确的记忆（Lachman et al.，1979）。一旦被试将这个故事与他们存储在记忆中的医院手术图式联系起来，他们就会觉得自己“记得”图式中的标签，而这些在所读内容中并没有出现过。因此，在图式帮助我们组织信息的同时，它们也增加了编码和提取中出现错误的可能性——这可能会使人产生错误记忆，因为我们会无意识地修改记忆信息，使其更符合我们基于图式而形成的预期。
p116.en: While reading the story as a medical story would make it easier to understand, it would also lead to an inaccurate memory of what was being tried (Lachman et al., 1979). Once they have been tried to link the story to the hospital surgery pattern that they have stored in their memory, they feel that they “remember” the labels in the pattern, which have not appeared in the reading. Thus, while the diagrams help us organize the information, they add to the possibility of errors in the coding and extraction — which may create a false memory, because we will unwittingly modify the memory information to make it more in line with our expectations based on the pattern.

p117.original: 从上述内容中你可以看到，图式如何在错误记忆中发挥关键作用：当回忆一个情境或事件时，我们会根据自己的预期来填补记忆的空白，但我们往往意识不到这种现象的存在。从好的一面看，图式通常是长时记忆的重要辅助工具，它给我们一个现成的框架来帮助我们理解新信息。但问题是，我们通常不知道对一件事的记忆是基于准确的信息，还是会包含我们基于图式和假设无意识地填补的信息。
p117.en: From the above, you can see how the pattern plays a key role in the wrong memory: when we remember a situation or event, we fill the gap in memory according to our expectations, but we are often unaware of the existence of this phenomenon. On the positive side, the diagram is usually an important aid for long-term memory, providing us with an off-the-shelf framework to help us understand new information. But the question is whether we usually do not know whether the memory of one thing is based on accurate information or whether it contains information that we inadvertently fill out on the basis of patterns and assumptions.

p118.original: 早期记忆 大多数人都很难记住自己在3岁之前发生过的事情，这种现象被称为童年期遗忘（childhood amnesia）。这一现象表明年幼儿的情景记忆能力有限。然而，早在3岁之前，或许从出生的那一刻起，儿童就已经开始学习了。我们根据婴儿能够学习辨认父母的面孔或幼儿能进行语言学习的现象就能证明这一点。因此我们知道，年幼的儿童至少可以进行语义记忆和程序性记忆。
p118.en: Early memory is difficult for most people to remember what happened before they were three years old, a phenomenon known as childhood forgotten (childhood amnesia). This phenomenon indicates limited situational memory of young children. However, children started learning well before the age of three, perhaps from the moment of birth. This can be demonstrated by the fact that a child can learn to recognize the face of his or her parents or that a young child can learn the language. We therefore know that at least a child can have semantic and procedural memory.

p119.original: 直到不久前，心理学家都还认为发生童年期遗忘是因为年幼儿童的大脑还未形成构建情景记忆所需的神经联结。然而，从现有的研究中我们知道，大脑在生命开始的第一个年末就已经开始建立必要的神经回路了。例如，认知科学家发现，9个月大的幼儿已经表现出了具有情景记忆的一些迹象，他们能够模仿一段时间之前观察到的行为（Bauer et al.，2003）。既然如此，你为什么不记得为你举办的第一个生日聚会呢？造成这一结果的部分原因可能是婴儿缺乏基本的语言技能（用于记忆的言语编码）和自我意识（自我意识作为自我参考点对个体发展而言非常必要，但一般到2岁左右才会形成），以及缺乏较年长的儿童和成年人所用的复杂图式来帮助自己进行记忆。
p119.en: Until recently, psychologists had also argued that childhood forgotten because young children's brains had not yet formed the neurolinks needed to construct scenario memory. However, from the existing research, we know that the brain has begun to build the necessary nerve circuits at the end of the first year of life. For example, cognitive scientists have found that nine-month-old children have shown some signs of scenario memory that they can imitate the behaviour observed some time ago (Bauer et al., 2003). Then why don't you remember your first birthday party? Part of the reason for this result may be the lack of basic language skills (coding for memory) and self-awareness (self-awareness as a self-reference point is necessary for individual development, but generally not until around the age of two), as well as the lack of complex images used by older children and adults to help them to remember.

p120.original: 文化背景也会影响人们的早期记忆。例如，新西兰的毛利人最早能回忆起2.5岁时的记忆，而韩国的成年人很少能记起4岁之前的事情。这种差异似乎取决于文化环境在多大程度上鼓励孩子们详细地讲述自己的生活。对孩子的养育“精雕细琢”的父母会花很多时间鼓励孩子谈论他们的日常经历，这似乎帮助儿童巩固了他们的早期记忆，使他们能够将这些记忆保持到成年阶段（Leichtman，2006；Winerman，2005a）。你可以利用上述信息来改善自己的学习和记忆。例如，通过谈论你正在学习的东西来为它创造更深刻的记忆！
p120.en: Cultural background can also affect people's early memories. For example, Maori in New Zealand can recall the memory of 2.5 years of age at the earliest, while adults in Korea rarely remember what happened before the age of 4. This difference seems to depend on the extent to which cultural environments encourage children to describe their lives in detail. Parents with “scrutinizing” parenting spend a lot of time encouraging children to talk about their daily experiences, which seems to help them consolidate their early memories and enable them to keep them in adulthood (Leichtman, 2006); Winerman, 2005a. You can use this information to improve your learning and memory. For example, by talking about what you're learning to create deeper memories for it!

p122.original: 一个多世纪以来，科学家们一直在寻找人们的记忆痕迹（engram），即长时记忆的生物基础。他们采用的一种策略是寻找大脑用来形成记忆的神经回路。另一种策略是在突触水平上寻找可能代表神经细胞内部生理记忆痕迹的生物化学变化。对一位名为H.M.的悲剧人物进行的研究使用了第一种策略。
p122.en: For more than a century, scientists have been looking for people's memory marks (engram), the biological foundation of long-term memory. One of the strategies they use is to find the neuropaths that the brain uses to form memory. Another strategy is to find biochemical changes at synaptic levels that may represent signs of physical memory within the nervous cell. The first strategy was used in the study of a tragic figure named H.M.

p123.original: 个案H.M.的启示 1953年，年轻的亨利·莫莱森（Henry Molaison）失去了形成新记忆的大部分能力，这是因治疗他频繁发作的癫痫疾病而不得不进行的一次实验性大脑手术所导致的后果（Corkin，2002；Hilts，1995）。从那以后，亨利（为了保护他的隐私，在他余生中，科学界只知道他的名字是H.M.）几乎完全无法对他生活中发生的事形成新的记忆。这种记忆障碍严重到他无法辨认在术后的几十年里是谁在照顾他。
p123.en: The revelation of case H.M., in 1953, young Henry Molaison lost most of his ability to form new memories as a result of an experimental brain surgery that had to be performed to treat his frequent epilepsy (Corkin, 2002); Hilts, 1995. Since then, Henry (who, for the rest of his life, the scientific community knew only that his name was H.M.) has been virtually unable to develop a new memory of what happened in his life. This memory disorder is so serious that he cannot identify who took care of him for decades after the operation.

p124.original: 值得注意的是，H.M.能回忆起手术前发生的事件，但新的经历在他将其存储到长时记忆之前就会消失。所以他对“9·11”事件、月球登陆事件和计算机革命一无所知。他不记得他早餐吃了什么，也不记得2分钟前离开的访客的名字。讽刺的是，他为数不多能记住的事情之一就是他有记忆问题。即使如此，当他从镜子中看到一张衰老的脸时还是会感到有点惊讶，他仍以为自己是1953年的那个年轻人（Milner et al.，1968；Rosenzweig，1992）。然而，在他经历的漫长磨难中，他始终能保持良好的精神状态，并愿意配合心理学家布伦达·米尔纳（Brenda Milner）开展工作，不过即使在与她共事多年后，他仍不认得她。
p124.en: It is noteworthy that H.M. can recall events before the operation, but that new experiences will disappear before he can store them for long. So he knew nothing about the events of 11 September, the landing of the Moon and the computer revolution. He did not remember what he had at breakfast or the names of the visitors who had left two minutes earlier. Ironically, one of the few things he can remember is that he has memory problems. Even so, he was surprised when he saw an ageing face in the mirror, and still thought he was the young man in 1953 (Milner et al., 1968); Rosenzweig, 1992. However, during his long ordeal, he remained in a good mental state and was willing to work with the psychologist Brenda Milner, although he still did not recognize her even after many years of working with her.

p125.original: H.M.的医疗记录中显示他的记忆障碍是顺行性遗忘症（anterograde amnesia）。从认知功能的角度来看，H.M.将新的概念和经历从工作记忆中输入长时记忆中的能力受到了严重的损害（Scoville & Milner，1957）。从生理学角度来看，他的双侧大脑的海马和杏仁核被移除是导致这个病症形成的原因。
p125.en: H.M.'s medical records show that his memory impairment is anchovious oblivion (anterograde amnesia). From a cognitive point of view, H.M.'s ability to input new concepts and experiences from work memory into long-term memory has been severely compromised (Scoville & Miller, 1957). From a physiological point of view, the removal of the hippos and almonds from his double brain is the cause of the disease.

p126.original: 当H. M.照镜子时，他的年龄让自己感到吃惊，因为自从他年轻时做过脑部手术，他对之后的数年岁月都没有任何记忆。
p126.en: When H.M. looked in the mirror, his age surprised him, since he had had brain surgery since he was young and had no memory of the years that followed.

p127.original: 我们从H.M.的案例中可以得到什么启发？从生物基础的角度来讲，这个案例告诉我们，海马和杏仁核对于形成新的陈述性记忆至关重要，尽管它们似乎在提取旧的（已记住的）记忆的过程中没有发挥作用（Bechara et al.，1995；Wirth et al.，2003）。而且，我们稍后会看到，H.M.的案例帮助我们理解了程序性记忆与陈述性记忆之间的区别。值得注意的是，H.M.对自己的病情仍能保持乐观的态度，甚至还会拿自己的记忆障碍来开玩笑。但具有讽刺意味的是，这种积极的性格可能部分源自杏仁核的移除（Corkin，2002）。
p127.en: What inspiration can we draw from the case of H.M.? From a biological standpoint, this case tells us that seahorses and almond cores are essential for the formation of new narrative memories, although they appear to have been ineffective in extracting old (remembered) memories (Bechara et al., 1995); Wirth et al., 2003). Moreover, as we will see later, the case of H.M. has helped us to understand the difference between procedural memory and narrative memory. It is noteworthy that H.M. remains optimistic about his condition and even makes fun of his memory impairments. But ironically, this positive character may be partly due to the removal of almonds (Corkin, 2002).

p128.original: 与长时记忆相关的大脑区域 在过去的20年里，神经科学家们已经在H.M.案例给我们提供的人类记忆信息的图景上增加了很多内容。我们现在知道海马与阿尔茨海默病有关，阿尔茨海默病也包括丧失了形成新的陈述性记忆的能力。神经科学家还发现，邻近海马的杏仁核会加工具有强烈情感联系的记忆（Bechara et al.，1995）。这些情感联系似乎有助于人们快速通达并提取记忆（Dolan，2002）。因此，对于那些经历过暴力袭击事件的士兵和人们所报告的持续令人不安的记忆，杏仁核在其中起着一定作用。在某些案例中，这些记忆令人感到十分烦扰，以至于构成了所谓的创伤后应激障碍（posttraumatic stress disorder，PTSD）。重要的是，这种情感记忆的生物基础会导致大多数创伤记忆长期保存在大脑中。
p128.en: The brain regions associated with long-term memory have, over the past 20 years, been significantly more informative by neuroscientists in the picture of the information that H.M. has given us about human memory. We now know that Hema is associated with Alzheimer's disease, which also includes the loss of the ability to develop new narrative memory. Neuroscientists also found that almond nuclei near the hippos process memory with strong emotional connections (Bechara et al., 1995). These emotional connections seem to help people quickly reach and extract their memories (Dolan, 2002). Thus, almond cores play a role in the continued disturbing memory of soldiers who have experienced violent attacks and those who have been reported. In some cases, these memories are so disturbing that they constitute so-called post-traumatic stress disorder (posttraumatic stress disorder, PTSD). It is important that the biological basis of this emotional memory leads to the long-term retention of most traumatic memories in the brain.

p129.original: 那么，记忆是存储在海马和杏仁核里吗？并不是。对事件和信息的记忆（陈述性记忆）实际上是存储在整个大脑皮层中，不同的记忆片段分别存储在最初加工某一特定感觉信号的大脑皮层中。因此，就拿你去年夏天在海滩度过的美好假期的记忆来说，其中的视觉记忆存储在你的视觉皮层中，而声音则存储在听觉皮层中，对气味的记忆则存储在嗅球中，对事件顺序的记忆则存储在额叶中，等等。并且，如果你在度假的过程中学会了冲浪，那么这段记忆就会与小脑和运动皮层联系在一起——就像其他包括身体运动和肌肉记忆的程序性记忆一样。
p129.en: So, are the memories stored in the seahorse and almond cores? Not really. The memory of events and information (expressive memory) is actually stored throughout the cortex of the brain, with different memories stored separately in the cortex of the brain initially processing a particular sensory signal. So, for the memory of the wonderful vacation you spent on the beach last summer, the visual memory is stored in your visual cortex, the sound is stored in the hearing cortex, the smell is stored in the sniffing ball, the sequence of events is stored in the forehead, etc. And if you learn to surf during your vacation, then this memory is linked to the small brain and the motor cortex -- just like other procedural memories that include physical motion and muscle memory.

p130.original: 你可能会想，这些记忆碎片是如何正确地整合起来的？（换句话说，冲浪的记忆是如何与其他在海滩度假的记忆相结合，而不是与你上次看牙医的记忆相结合呢？）虽然这一神奇本领的技术细节对神经科学家来说仍然是个谜，但我们的确知道有部分脑区会在其中发挥重要作用。在被称为记忆巩固（consolidation）的过程中，记忆能够在海马的帮助下逐渐变得更加持久。本质上讲，每次当我们提取一段新的陈述性记忆时，存储在各个脑区中的有关这段记忆的片段就会在海马中汇集起来，海马以某种方式对它们进行整理，并将相关的片段重新组合成连贯的记忆。每次提取都会使特定记忆的神经通路得到加强。最终，某一段记忆不需要依靠海马就能自动整合在一起。到那时，这段记忆中的任何一个片段（如海洋的气味）都足以激活完整的记忆。
p130.en: You might wonder how these memory fragments were properly integrated. (In other words, how do surfing memories combine with other beach vacation memories rather than with the memories of your last dentist? Although the technical details of this magic technique remain a mystery for neuroscientists, we do know that some of the brain regions will play an important role in it. In the process known as memory consolidation, memory can gradually become more durable with the help of sea horses. In essence, each time we extract a new narrative memory, the fragments of that memory stored in the various brain regions are gathered in the sea horses, which sort them out in one way or another and re-composed the relevant fragments into a coherent memory. Each extraction strengthens the neuropaths of specific memories. Ultimately, a certain memory does not need to rely on seahorses to be automatically integrated. By that time, any part of this memory (e.g. the smell of the ocean) would be sufficient to activate the full memory.

p131.original: 在对记忆存储和巩固有了更多了解后，我们就能知道为什么H.M.不能形成新的陈述性记忆了，在切除了海马后，他的大脑就缺少执行这些加工所需的硬件。由于旧的记忆已经被多次巩固，因此不需要依靠海马就能对完整的记忆进行提取，所以他仍可以回忆起这些旧的记忆。这也解释了为什么他具备形成新的程序性记忆的能力，因为这些记忆的形成不需要海马的参与。而且，研究报告称，对于我们这些拥有完整海马的人来说，如果能将新的经历与现有的记忆图式关联，那么我们对这些记忆的巩固速度就会更快（Squire，2007；Tse et al.，2007），这也从生物基础的角度解释了为什么精细复述和加工深度能够帮助我们创造更持久的记忆。
p131.en: With more knowledge of memory storage and consolidation, we can see why H.M. can't create new narrative memories, and after removing the sea horses, his brain lacks the hardware necessary to carry out these processes. Since old memories have been consolidated many times, and thus the full memory cannot be extracted from the seahorse, he can still recall them. This explains why he has the capacity to develop new procedural memories, which do not require the involvement of sea horses. Moreover, the study reports that for us who have complete sea horses, we will be able to consolidate these memories faster if new experiences are linked to existing memory patterns (Squire, 2007); Tse et al., 2007), which also explains from the biological basis point of view why finely recapitulated and processed depths can help us create more sustainable memories.

p132.original: 记忆、神经元和突触 在电视连续剧和电影中经常会出现一个人在遭受打击或头部受伤后患上失忆症（失去记忆）的情节，但研究结果是否支持这种好莱坞式的神经科学呢？在单个神经元水平上，记忆最初只是在突触上形成的脆弱的化学痕迹，随着时间的推移，经过反复提取和细化的记忆会被巩固为更持久的突触变化。在巩固的过程中，记忆非常容易受到新的经历、特定的药物或头部撞击的干扰（Doyère et al.，2007）。如果一个人出现严重的失忆现象，则会被诊断为逆行性遗忘症（retrograde amnesia）。（请注意，逆行性遗忘症与H.M.患有的顺行性遗忘症正好相反。）
p132.en: Memory, neurons, and synapses are common in television series and movies when a person suffers from amnesia after being hit or a head injury, but does the results support this Hollywood-style neuroscience? At individual neurons levels, memory is initially a fragile chemical trace of synapse, and over time, repeated extraction and refinement of memory can be consolidated into more lasting synapses. In the consolidation process, memory is highly vulnerable to new experiences, specific drugs or head impact (Doyère et al., 2007). If a person suffers from severe amnesia, it is diagnosed as a retrograde amnesia. (Note that retrograde oblivion is the opposite of H.M.'s deviant oblivion. I don't think so.

p133.original: 因此，在巩固过程中，记忆可能会被增强或减弱。此外，人的情绪状态可以影响这一巩固过程，尽管积极与消极这两种不同的情绪对注意和记忆的影响有很大的不同。如果你感到愉快，那么你就会倾向于广泛地注意当前的情况并记住“全局”。但是如果你遭到抢劫并被枪指着时，你很可能只会注意到枪，而不太会关注抢劫者的外貌细节。总体来说，我们可以认为情绪唤醒能让我们形成最生动但不是最准确的记忆：愉快记忆的范围往往更大，因为消极情绪往往会限制我们在记忆时的关注点（Dingfelder，2005；Levine & Bluck，2004）。
p133.en: Thus, in the consolidation process, memory may be enhanced or weakened. Moreover, the emotional state of the human person can influence this consolidation process, although the impact on attention and memory of both positive and negative sentiments is very different. If you are happy, then you tend to pay broad attention to the current situation and to remember “the whole picture”. But if you were robbed and pointed at a gun, you would probably have only noticed the gun and not paid much attention to the details of the robber's appearance. In general, we can assume that emotional awakening can give us the most vivid, but not the most accurate, memory: the range of happy memories is often greater, because negative emotions tend to limit our focus on memory (Dingfeld, 2005); Levine & Black, 2004.

p134.original: 在结束这一学习阶段的内容之前，我们应该注意到，从进化的视角来看，情绪在记忆中起着高度适应性的作用（见图5-10）。例如，如果你在野外遇到一头熊之后还能活下来，那么这段让你感到恐惧的经历很可能会使你记得以后要避开熊。在这一点上，我们应该感谢杏仁核，以及与情绪相关的化学物质，如肾上腺素和某些应激激素。在它们的共同作用下，通过建立“超强”的情绪联结，增强对那些带有强烈情绪唤醒经历的记忆（McGaugh，2000）。
p134.en: Before concluding this learning phase, we should note that from an evolutionary perspective, emotions play a highly adaptable role in memory (see figure 5-10). For example, if you survive meeting a bear in the field, this experience that scares you is likely to remind you of avoiding the bear later. In that regard, we should thank almond cores and emotional-related chemicals, such as adrenaline and certain stress hormones. Together, they have enhanced memory of those who have a strong emotional awakening experience by creating a “super-strong” emotional bond (McGaugh, 2000).

p136.original: 注：应激事件会触发大脑释放应激激素，这些激素作用于杏仁核与海马，从而加强对该事件的情绪记忆。因此，与那些认为我们会忘记或压抑有关应激事件记忆的流行观点相反，我们更有可能会记住它们。
p136.en: Note: The stress event triggers the brain to release stress hormones, which act on almonds and hippos, thus enhancing emotional memory of the event. Therefore, contrary to the prevailing perception that we will forget or suppress the memory of stressful events, we are more likely to remember them.

p137.original: 心理学很有用 闪光灯记忆：当……的时候，你在哪儿
p137.en: Psychology works. Flash memory: where were you when...

p138.original: 对大多数人来说，拥有最接近“摄影式记忆”的能力就是闪光灯记忆（flashbulb memory），即对一件重要且充满情绪的事件拥有非常清晰的记忆（Brown & Kulik，1977）。你可能会有这样几次回忆：一次毕业典礼、一场悲惨的事故、一次死亡事件或一场大胜利。闪光灯记忆就好像你能在脑海里瞬间画出那些引人注目的场景一样。（“闪光灯记忆”是在拍摄每张照片都需要一个闪光灯的时期被创造出来的一个词。）闪光灯记忆最典型的特征就是记忆的来源（Davidson et al.，2005）：这些生动的记忆画面描绘了人们在接受这些消息时所处的场景，他们当时在做什么，以及他们所感受到的情绪状态。
p138.en: For most people, the ability to have the closest “photographic memory” is the flashbulb memory, which is very clear about an event that is important and emotional (Brown & Kulik, 1977). You may have a few memories: a graduation ceremony, a tragic accident, a death or a great victory. The flashlight memories are like you can draw dramatic scenes in your head. (“The flashlight memory” is a word created during a time when each photo requires a flash light. The most typical feature of flashlight memories is their source (Davidson et al., 2005): These vivid images of memories depict people's situation when they receive these messages, what they were doing, and the emotional state they felt.

p139.original: 许多人都会对新闻中充满情绪性的事件形成闪光灯记忆，例如，波士顿马拉松爆炸案、“9·11”事件，或者巴拉克·奥巴马（Barack Obama）当选美国总统（Pillemer，1984；Schmolck et al.，2000）。认知心理学家对这些现实中自然发生的事件进行研究，以寻找下面这个重要问题的答案：闪光灯记忆的情绪性是否会影响记忆的准确性？
p139.en: Many people have flashlights of emotional events in the news, such as the Boston Marathon bombing, the events of 11 September, or Barack Obama's election to the United States presidency (Pillemer, 1984); Schmolck et al., 2000. Cognitive psychologists study the natural events in these realities to find answers to the crucial question: Will the emotionality of flashlight memories affect the accuracy of memory?

p140.original: 杜克大学（Duke University）的一项研究收集了学生对“9·11”事件发生后第二天的记忆（Talarico & Rubin，2003）。研究人员还从同一批被试那里收集了他们关于日常事件的记忆。32 周后，研究人员对被试的记忆准确性进行了测试。结果如何呢？平均而言，闪光灯记忆并不比日常记忆更准确，这两种记忆的准确性都会随着时间的推移而下降。然而，重要的是，被试对闪光灯记忆的准确性非常有信心：相比于日常记忆，这些学生对他们闪光灯记忆的准确性更有信心，但这是错误的！值得注意的是，人们对闪光灯记忆的信心水平与最初经历闪光灯事件时的情绪唤醒水平相关。其他研究也证明了这一观点，即情绪唤醒虽然会增加记忆的生动性，但并不一定会增加记忆的准确性。
p140.en: A study by Duke University collected students' memories of the day after the events of 11 September (Talarico & Rubin, 2003). Researchers also collected their memories of everyday events from the same group of people who were tested. After a week, researchers tested the accuracy of the trial memory. How'd it go? On average, flashlight memories are no more accurate than routine memories, and both are less accurate over time. However, what is important is that they have great confidence in the accuracy of flashlight memories: these students have greater confidence in the accuracy of their flashlight memories than they do in everyday memory, but this is wrong! It is noteworthy that the level of confidence in flashlight memory is related to the level of emotional awakening during the initial flash event. Other studies have also confirmed the view that emotional awakening, while adding to the vividness of memory, does not necessarily increase its accuracy.

p141.original: 你还记得2008年奥巴马赢得美国总统大选时，你在哪里，当时感觉如何吗？很有可能，你的闪光灯记忆并不像你想象的那么准确。
p141.en: Do you remember where you were when Obama won the United States presidential election in 2008, and how you felt? Most likely, your flashlight memories are not as accurate as you think.

p142.original: 鉴于已经有强有力的证据支持个人对情绪事件的回想会被增强，那么我们如何理解情绪唤醒在闪光灯记忆中的独特作用呢？首先，我们必须注意到，闪光灯记忆不同于与个人有关的创伤性事件的记忆。闪光灯记忆的内容通常是公众熟知的、广泛传播的事件，而对于个体而言，我们可能并没有亲身参与到这种情境中。公共事件很可能会有铺天盖地的新闻报道，被广泛讨论并频繁转述。在这些频繁的讲述中，事件的细节可能会被扭曲。
p142.en: Given that there is already strong evidence to support an increase in individual perceptions of emotional events, how do we understand the unique role of emotional awakening in flashlight memories? First, we must note that flashlight memories differ from memories of traumatic events related to individuals. The content of flashlight memories is usually a well-known, widely disseminated event, and for individuals we may not be personally involved in this situation. Public events are likely to be well-spreaded, widely discussed and frequently relayed. In these frequent accounts, the details of the incident may be distorted.

p143.original: 俗话说，细节决定成败。有关闪光灯记忆的研究表明，人们往往会对某些生动的细节记得非常准确，但是随着时间的推移，其他同样生动的细节就记得没那么准确了。对以色列学生进行的一项研究发现，在以色列总理伊扎克·拉宾（Itzhak Rabin）被暗杀后，被生动报告的记忆中只有大约三分之二在11个月后仍然准确（Nachson & Zelig，2003）——尽管人们对错误记忆的信心仍然很高。正如前所述，创伤性事件会使我们的注意范围变得狭窄；因此，我们只会对特定的细节进行编码，然后完全无意识地用我们从他人那里听到的细节，或者我们认为符合该事件图式的一些细节来填充我们的记忆框架。
p143.en: As they say, the details determine success or failure. Studies on flashlight memory suggest that some vivid details are often well remembered, but other equally vivid details are less accurate over time. A study of Israeli students found that only about two thirds of the vividly reported memories after the assassination of Israeli Prime Minister Itzhak Rabin remained accurate after 11 months (Nachson & Zelig, 2003) — although confidence in false memories remains high. As mentioned earlier, traumatic events narrow our focus; We will therefore only encode specific details and then, completely unconsciously, fill our memory framework with details we hear from others, or some details that we believe fit the pattern of the event.

p144.original: 尽管这样可能会导致记忆错误，但错误地相信记忆的准确性可能具有适应性意义。进化心理学家认为，当人们面对压力时，能否迅速而自信地做出选择可能会决定生死（Poldrack et al.，2008）。从这个角度来说，细节可能决定成败。
p144.en: While this may lead to memory errors, there is a false belief that memory accuracy may be adaptive. Evolutionary psychologists believe that when people face stress, the ability to make a quick and confident choice may determine whether they live or die (Poldrack et al., 2008). From this perspective, details may determine success or failure.
